P1.Title: Novelist; Philosopher; Founder of Objectivism
P1.Bio: Ayn Rand (born Alisa Rosenbaum) was a Russian-American novelist and philosopher who originated Objectivism. Born in St. Petersburg in 1905, she witnessed the Russian Revolution as a teenager and condemned communism as immoral. In 1926 she fled to America, adopting the pen name Ayn Rand. Her novels — particularly The Fountainhead (1943) and Atlas Shrugged (1957) — present heroic, egoistic characters living by reason and rational self-interest. Until her death in 1982 she wrote extensively across all five branches of philosophy.
P1.Major works: We the Living (1936); Anthem (1938); The Fountainhead (1943); Atlas Shrugged (1957); For the New Intellectual (1961); The Virtue of Selfishness (1964); Capitalism: The Unknown Ideal (1966); Introduction to Objectivist Epistemology (1966); The Romantic Manifesto (1969); Philosophy: Who Needs It (1982)

P2.Bio: Leonard Peikoff has spent more than sixty years studying, teaching, and applying the philosophy of Ayn Rand. Born in Winnipeg, Canada, he first met Rand in 1951 when he was seventeen. He studied philosophy at New York University and taught at several colleges from 1957 to 1973. His 1976 lecture course was endorsed by Rand herself. On her death in 1982 she named him heir to her estate. He founded the Ayn Rand Institute in 1985 and is today the world's preeminent authority on Objectivism.

In later life he took up painting, with Rand proudly displaying his canvases in their New York apartment.

P100.Name: Nathaniel Branden
P100.Title: Psychologist; Author; Lecturer
P100.Bio: Nathaniel Branden (born Nathan Blumenthal) was a Canadian-American psychologist and the foremost intellectual associate of Ayn Rand for nearly two decades. He met Rand in 1950 when he was nineteen and she was his philosophical mentor. Together they founded the Nathaniel Branden Institute (NBI) in 1958, through which Objectivism was widely disseminated via lectures across North America in the 1960s. Their romantic relationship and professional collaboration ended in 1968 in a permanent break. He went on to become a pioneering psychologist in the self-esteem movement. His memoir My Years with Ayn Rand (1999) is a key primary source on Rand's life and circle.
P100.Major works: The Psychology of Self-Esteem (1969); Breaking Free (1970); The Disowned Self (1971); Honoring the Self (1983); The Six Pillars of Self-Esteem (1994); My Years with Ayn Rand (1999)

P102.Bio: David Kelley is a philosopher and the founder of The Atlas Society (originally the Institute for Objectivist Studies, founded 1990). His split from the Ayn Rand Institute in 1990, following a dispute with Leonard Peikoff over speaking at non-Objectivist forums, led to the creation of the independent Objectivist movement. He developed the concept of "open Objectivism," holding that Rand's philosophy should be engaged critically and expanded through ongoing scholarship rather than treated as a closed system.

Consulting producer of the Atlas Shrugged films and one of the screenwriters of Atlas Shrugged: Part II (and drafted the Part III screenplay). Wrote and directed a stage adaptation of Anthem.
